Executive Summary

Gold had the biggest run of its modern history. It gained 64% in 2025 and 27% in January 2026, a parabolic blow-off that peaked at 5,626.8 (/GC) on Jan 29. Ten months later it is down 31% at 3,884.7, and GLD (≈$352) has just broken below its 52-week low of $354.67. The cause is not a collapse in demand: central banks bought 321 tonnes in Q3, +42% y/y. The cause is a regime change in the price of money. The Fed resumed hiking in September, a December hike is now almost fully priced, the dollar is firm, and an AI-led equity sell-off is forcing liquidity sales.

Technically, gold is sitting on the 61.8% retracement (3,900.3) of the 2025 breakout leg, a shelf it has now tested three times (July, Oct 30, Nov 11). Each bounce off it has been weaker than the last: lower highs at 4,755 (Aug), then 4,157.7 (Nov). Daily trend tools are bearish across the board, and your FDTS+MACD system flipped to SELL today at 3,883.90. Momentum oscillators are deeply oversold (WRP −93 daily, −96 hourly), and Nov 11 left a buying tail at 3,850.

FazDane Bottom Line

Bearish structure on an oversold shelf. A weekly close below 3,856.7 (GLD ~$350) opens the next step down to 3,613 → 3,500 (GLD $328 → $317), where both the option-implied 1σ cone and several analyst targets sit. A reclaim of 3,993–4,014 (GLD $362–364) would neutralize the breakdown. The ±1σ cone into the Dec 18 expiry is 3,613–4,176 /GC (GLD $328–$379).

The Paradox Explained

Gold is falling during a war, persistent inflation and an equity sell-off, the textbook reasons to own it. The explanation is sequencing. The war raised oil, oil raised inflation, and inflation turned the Fed from cutting to hiking. Hiking raised real yields and the dollar, which is gold's biggest headwind. The safe-haven bid exists, but it is losing to the rate channel. Central banks are the one buyer that does not care about real yields, which is why the decline has been orderly rather than a collapse.

Chart 1 — Secular Structure (Max Weekly)

Figure 1: /GC weekly chart, 1998–present. The green dotted line marks the 2011–2023 resistance (~1,900–2,075) that capped gold for 12 years. The Fibonacci retracement runs from the 2025 breakout base (2,833.1) to the January 2026 record (5,626.8): 38.2% 4,559.6 · 50% 4,230 · 61.8% 3,900.3.

The secular picture is still bullish. Gold spent 12 years building a base under ~2,075, broke out in 2024 and went vertical. The current decline is a retracement of the final, parabolic leg (2,833 → 5,627). The 61.8% level is where a healthy secular trend should hold. Parabolic advances often retrace more than 61.8%, though, and a full round-trip to the base of the leg (~2,833 / GLD ~257) would still leave the 2024 breakout intact. That is the long-term bull case's margin of safety, not a target.

Chart 2 — 5-Year Weekly: The Triple Test

Figure 2: /GC 5-year weekly chart (percent scale). Week of Nov 9: O 4,074.3 · H 4,157.7 · L 3,856.7 · C 3,884.2. The 61.8% level (3,900.3) has been tested three times since July. Rally highs: 5,626.8 (Jan) → ~5,450 (Mar) → ~4,890 (Apr) → 4,755 (Aug) → 4,157.7 (Nov).

This week's candle is bearish. It opened at 4,074 and was rejected at 4,157.7, then closed at 3,884, near the low and below the 61.8% level. The structure since March is a series of lower highs into a flat shelf, a descending triangle. That pattern is bearish continuation more often than not. A weekly close below 3,856.7 would complete it. The textbook measured move (Aug high 4,755 − shelf 3,870 ≈ 885) points as low as ~2,985, but we treat that as an outer bound. The nearer and more credible magnet is the 2025 congestion zone around 3,300–3,500, where analyst targets cluster.

The counter-argument: a level that holds three times on shrinking rallies can also be accumulation by price-insensitive buyers, and the Q3 central-bank data fit that reading. A weekly close back above 3,993 would invalidate the breakdown.

Historical Rhyme Worth Watching

In December 2015, gold made its cycle low (~$1,046) within a day of the Fed's first hike, then rallied ~30% over the following months. Markets often price a hike fully before it happens and then "sell the rumor, buy the fact." With December hike odds near 100%, the December FOMC is the most likely window for a durable low, if the Fed signals the hike is one-and-done. A hawkish dot plot would instead support Scenario B.

Summary & Actionable Conclusions
Cause: The Fed, Not Demand

Hikes since September, near-100% December odds and ~2.8% real yields outweigh war and inflation hedging. Liquidity selling from AI stocks adds to the pressure.

Floor: Central Banks

321t in Q3 (+42% y/y) and 675t YTD. Price-insensitive buyers are why this is a correction rather than a collapse.

Structure: Triple-Tested Shelf

The 61.8% level (3,900 / GLD 354) has held three times on weakening bounces, a descending triangle that is bearish until reclaimed.

Cone Ranges

±1σ: GLD $341–364 by Nov 20 · $328–379 by Dec 18 · $307–404 by Mar 19. Close-below-low odds ≈ 50/50.

Signals: Daily Sell, Hourly Oversold

FDTS SELL today; below all MAs and below value. WRP −93/−96 → a bounce to $362–364 is likely, but it is a test.

Plan: Wait for the Fact

Basing range 45% / breakdown 35% / reversal 20%. Accumulate at $317–328 or on a reclaim of $364; watch the December FOMC as the low window.
